GOLES: 0-1 Aitor Galarza, min. 27; 0-2Ekain, min.44; 1-2Diego Espejo, min.64; 2-2 Gothler, min.79. ÁRBITRO: Roberto Gonzalo (Comité de Castilla La Mancha. Tarjetas a los locales Bekhoucha y Nordin; y a los visitantes Álvaro Mateo, Unai García y Aitor Galarza. INCIDENCIAS: 4.500 espectadores en el estadio Francisco de la Hera Dos zarpazos visitantes antes del descanso El choque se torció pronto para los extremeños. En el minuto 28, Aitor Galarza abrió el marcador para poner el 0-1, premio a la capacidad del delantero vasco para generar peligro: acabó el encuentro como el jugador más incisivo de su equipo con cuatro remates y una valoración de 7.5. Justo antes del intermedio, en el 45, Ekain Azkune amplió distancias con el 0-2, dejando tocado a un Extremadura que se marchó al vestuario con una losa de dos goles pese a dominar la posesión. Los números del primer acto reflejaban la paradoja del partido: el Extremadura mandaba con el balón —acabaría el encuentro con un 54% de posesión y 401 pases por 358— pero el Real Unión golpeaba con una eficacia demoledora. De hecho, los txuri-urdin firmaron cinco disparos a puerta por solo tres de los locales, y sus goles esperados sobre tiro a puerta (1.74) superaron claramente a los del rival (1.05). La reacción local y el penalti providencial El técnico local movió el banquillo en el descanso con una doble sustitución, dando entrada a Nordin Al Lal y a Diego Díaz por Yael Ballesteros y Kike Márquez. El cambio redibujó el partido. Y en el 52 llegó el momento que pudo sentenciar: tras una revisión del VAR, el Real Unión dispuso de un penalti. Pero Unai García, el mejor valorado del encuentro con un 7.9 pese a todo, lo falló. El guardameta local David Pinto Robador adivinó las intenciones y detuvo la pena máxima, una de sus tres paradas en una actuación de nota (7.2). Perdonado el 0-3, el Extremadura resucitó. En el minuto 65, el central Diego Espejo —excelente, con un 7.7 de valoración y tres pases clave desde atrás— recortó distancias con el 1-2. El conjunto de Almendralejo olió la sangre y volcó su fútbol sobre la meta de Lander Emery, que acabó con unos goles evitados de -0.95, síntoma de que su equipo sufrió más de lo que el marcador llegó a reflejar. El empate llegó en el 80. Alfred Gøthler, que apenas llevaba cinco minutos sobre el césped tras sustituir a Iker Burgos, remató para firmar el 2-2 definitivo con asistencia de Diego Díaz. El delantero danés, el futbolista de mayor valor de mercado del once local, necesitó apenas quince minutos para dejar su sello: 7.6 de valoración y un gol que valió un punto de oro. Un final de infarto con el VAR de protagonista El tramo final fue un vendaval. En el minuto 90, el videoarbitraje entró en escena hasta en dos ocasiones: primero no señaló un penalti reclamado por Rodrigo Escudero, y después anuló lo que habría sido el 3-2 de Luis Morcillo por fuera de juego. El Extremadura se quedó con la miel en los labios de una remontada completa, pero pudo respirar tras haber estado contra las cuerdas durante gran parte del encuentro. Las estadísticas avalan el dominio final de los locales: 19 disparos por 11, siete córners por dos y, sobre todo, cinco ocasiones claras frente a una sola del rival. El Extremadura desperdició tres de esas grandes oportunidades, un dato que explica por qué un partido tan controlado estuvo a punto de saldarse con derrota. Lo que dice la clasificación El reparto mantiene a los dos equipos pegados en la zona media-baja del Grupo 1. El Real Unión Club es décimo con 10 puntos (2 victorias, 4 empates, 2 derrotas) tras ocho jornadas, mientras que el CD Extremadura ocupa la undécima plaza, también con 10 puntos pero con un balance de 3 triunfos, 1 empate y 4 derrotas. Ambos quedan muy lejos del liderato que ostenta el CD Lugo, imbatido con 22 puntos y siete victorias en ocho partidos. Para el Extremadura, el punto sabe a poco por las sensaciones finales pero mucho por cómo se obtuvo: remar dos goles en contra y salvar un penalti habla de carácter. Para el Real Unión, en cambio, es una oportunidad perdida: ganaba por 0-2, falló un penalti y se le escapó un triunfo que habría cambiado su semana. La regularidad de los empates —cuatro ya esta temporada— empieza a ser una seña de identidad incómoda para los vascos. Jugadores destacados El duelo tuvo varios protagonistas de nota alta. Unai García (7.9) fue el jugador más influyente del campo pese al penalti errado, con un despliegue físico notable (13 duelos ganados). Por el Extremadura, Diego Espejo (7.7) combinó gol y solvencia defensiva, mientras que Alfred Gøthler (7.6) resolvió desde el banquillo. Mención aparte para David Pinto Robador, cuya parada de penalti resultó, a la postre, tan decisiva como cualquiera de los cuatro goles. Un 2-2 justo en el reparto, pero con dos lecturas opuestas: euforia contenida en Almendralejo, frustración en Irún.

articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as Trinidad Chambliss Rises, Arch Manning Falls

articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning has lost his preseason status as a Heisman Trophy favorite after back-to-back losses to unranked teams.

Manning is +22500 to win the Heisman after Florida upset No. 7 Texas with a 27-24 win Saturday, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

No. 9 Ole Miss claimed a 31-3 blowout over No. 13 Missouri the same day to help make quarterback Trinidad Chambliss a top-five Heisman favorite.

Here's a look at the latest Heisman Trophy odds now that Manning has falling further out of the running to be celebrated as the top player in college football.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+3000)

Manning threw for 173 yards and a touchdown in Saturday's loss. Texas, which lost last weekend to Oklahoma, is the first team since 1961 to go from No. 1 in the AP Poll to losing to two unranked opponents.

Chambliss is +700 to win the Heisman after passing for 241 yards and three touchdowns in the blowout over Missouri.

Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor and Oregon quarterback have slipped behind other Heisman favorites after missing time due to respective foot and head injuries.

Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin and Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover, who ranked among Heisman favorites earlier this season, are also out of the top of the rankings after both struggling in a Saturday Buckeyes win.

Buckeyes wideout Smith recorded a season-low 68 receiving yards on four catches in the win but still remains the betting favorite to win the trophy.

Miami quarterback Darian Mensah could look to challenge Smith at the top of the betting odds with a strong performance in Saturday's home game against Florida State.

articles.title: Un golazo de Slavy hace justicia
articles.standfirst: El delantero de la Deportiva anotó el 1-1 que le da un punto a un conjunto berciano que fue mejor en la primera mitad y supo reponerse tras el gol de Carbonell
articles.summary: El delantero de la Deportiva anotó el 1-1 que le da un punto a un conjunto berciano que fue mejor en la primera mitad y supo reponerse tras el gol de Carbonell
articles.body: El Zamora CF y la SD Ponferradina se repartieron los puntos (1-1) en la octava jornada de la Primera Federación (Grupo 1), en un duelo del centro de la tabla resuelto a base de dos zarpazos en la segunda mitad y un guion que osciló entre la pegada local y la reacción visitante. Ante 3.018 espectadores, el choque confirmó lo igualado de un tramo medio de la clasificación donde ambos conjuntos conviven con 12 puntos, separados únicamente por el golaverage. FICHA TÉCNICA Zamora C. F. Iker Piedra; Diego Moreno, Luismi Luengo, Dufur, Aleix Gorjón, Vergés; Álex Hidalgo (Costa), Carlos Ramos, Iago Indias (Losada), Urzain; y Carbonell. –Entrenador: Óscar Cano. S. D. Ponferradina, Álex Domínguez; Emi Hernández (Calderón), Undabarrena, Jelbat, Aleix Roig (Sergio Nieto); San Emeterio, Borja Valle; Quicala Bari, Pablo Muñoz (Tounkara), José de León (Chibozo); y Óscar Vacas (Slavy). -Entrenador: Mehdi Nafti. Goles: 1-0: Carbonell (min 50); 1-1: Slavy (min. 74). Árbitro: Gonzalo González, asistido por Jabir Bouiri y Mohamed Boukili. Amonestó con tarjeta amarilla a los locales Ramos y Gorjón y al visitante Pablo Muñoz Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la 8ª jornada del campeonato nacional de Liga en el Grupo I de Primera Federación disputado en el Estadio Ruta de la Plata de Zamora. Un primer tiempo trabado y sin premio Los primeros 45 minutos se fueron al descanso con 0-0 en el marcador, reflejo de una fase inicial tacticamente cerrada. La Ponferradina manejó algo más el balón (54% de posesión frente al 46% local) y acumuló más llegadas al área rival, pero el Zamora se mostró más incisivo en sus acercamientos: el dato de goles esperados a puerta (1,58 por 0,73) revela que, cuando los de casa remataron entre palos, generaron mayor peligro real. La única amonestación del acto inicial cayó sobre el local Aleix Gorjón en el minuto 21. El resto fue un pulso de tanteo, con el guardameta visitante Alex Domínguez — autor de un notable 7,5 de valoración y de cuatro paradas — ya avisando de que iba a ser protagonista. Carbonell abre y Slavy iguala El partido se desató tras el intermedio. En el minuto 50, Javier Carbonell resolvió para adelantar al Zamora (1-0), colofón a la mejor actuación individual del encuentro: el delantero firmó un 8,0 de nota, tres remates —los tres a puerta—, una ocasión clara generada y un gol que premió su constante amenaza pese a tocar apenas 22 balones. La Ponferradina respondió con un movimiento desde el banquillo. Slavy había entrado en el 62 por Óscar Vacas y, once minutos después, en el 73, firmó el empate (1-1) tras asistencia de Pablo Muñoz. El tanto llegó poco después de una decisión del VAR en el 69 que afectó al propio delantero búlgaro. El suplente resolvió con eficacia su ocasión —0,43 de goles esperados en apenas 28 minutos— y dejó un 7,1 de valoración que justificó la apuesta del técnico visitante. A partir de ahí, el Zamón buscó recuperar la ventaja con una triple sustitución en el minuto 80 (Pau Mascaró, Isaiah Navarro y Guillem Rodríguez), pero el acierto de Domínguez bajo palos y la solidez defensiva visitante —con Aymane Jelbat firmando diez despejes— mantuvieron el reparto hasta el pitido final. Las claves estadísticas El 1-1 encaja con un partido parejo en casi todas las métricas. La Ponferradina remató más (13 por 10) y tuvo más posesión y pases completados (318 por 234), síntoma de su mayor control con el balón. El Zamora, en cambio, dominó la batalla física: ganó el 58% de los duelos, el 59% de los cuerpo a cuerpo en el suelo y completó 23 entradas por solo 11 de su rival, con un 57% de eficacia en el robo frente al 27% visitante. Ambos equipos repartieron ocasiones claras (2-2) y ambos las desperdiciaron por igual (2-2), lo que explica que ninguno lograra romper el empate en el tramo final. Los dos porteros firmaron cuatro paradas cada uno, pero el dato de goles evitados (0,58 de Domínguez frente a -0,27 de Iker Piedra) inclina ligeramente la balanza del rendimiento bajo palos hacia la portería visitante. En la pizarra, los visitantes alinearon un 4-2-3-1 y los locales un 3-4-3. Por el Zamora destacaron también el central Unai Dufur (7,3), con dos bloqueos y tres entradas ganadas, y el polivalente Eudald Vergés (7,2). En la Ponferradina, además de Domínguez, sobresalieron el capitán Eneko Undabarrena (7,0, 48 pases acertados de 52) y el dominicano José De León (7,1), autor de una ocasión clara creada y de dos remates a puerta antes de ser sustituido. Lo que deja en la clasificación El empate deja a ambos conjuntos empatados a 12 puntos tras ocho jornadas, con idéntico balance de tres victorias, tres empates y dos derrotas. El Zamora CF ocupa la sexta plaza con un golaverage de +2 (10 goles a favor, 8 en contra), mientras que la SD Ponferradina es séptima con diferencia de goles neutra (6-6), siendo precisamente su falta de pegada —solo seis tantos en ocho partidos, uno de los registros ofensivos más bajos de la zona alta— su principal asignatura pendiente. Por arriba, el Grupo 1 lo manda con autoridad el CD Lugo, único invicto con 22 puntos (siete victorias y un empate), seguido a distancia por UD Logroñés y Racing de Ferrol, ambos con 16. El pelotón que forman Zamora y Ponferradina, junto a Athletic Club B, CP Cacereño, Cultural Leonesa y Mirandés, mantiene con vida las aspiraciones de uno y otro de cara a la pelea por los puestos nobles, aunque el reparto de este sábado frena el impulso que ambos necesitaban para escalar posiciones. Con un punto que sabe a poco para los dos, Zamora y Ponferradina seguirán instalados en esa zona media donde cada jornada puede suponer un salto o una caída de varios puestos. El acierto de Carbonell y la respuesta de Slavy resumieron un duelo tan igualado como su resultado.

articles.title: La efectividad del Ibiza tumbó la ilusión local
articles.standfirst: El Águilas sigue en dinámica perdedora y no sale de la zona de descenso a Segunda RFEF
articles.summary: El Águilas sigue en dinámica perdedora y no sale de la zona de descenso a Segunda RFEF
articles.body: En el fútbol, la paciencia a veces se cobra intereses en el último suspiro. La UD Ibiza se marchó del feudo del CDA Águilas FC con un triunfo por 1-2 labrado en los compases finales de un duelo del Grupo 2 de Primera Federación que permaneció sin goles durante 73 minutos y que, de pronto, se convirtió en un vendaval. Tres tantos en los últimos diecisiete minutos, uno de ellos ya en el tiempo de descuento, resumieron un choque que los locales dominaron en ocasiones pero que los visitantes supieron rematar con oficio. FICHA TÉCNICA Águilas Fútbol Club, Salcedo; Johan Terranova, José Mas, Antonio Sánchez, Héctor Martínez (Collado, min.83); Yasser (Emilio de Teresa, min.71), Abenza, Serpeta (Adri Heredia, min.23), Josema Raigal; Javi Castedo (Lobede, min.83) y Gonzalo Serrano (Dani Merchán, min.71). Unión Deportiva Ibiza, Prieto; Almenara, Blasco, Erik Ruiz, Víctor García; Calavera, Pedro Ortiz (Lazo, min.81), Theo Valls (Fadel, min.86); Astals (Genaro, min.92), Ander Yoldi (Nsukula, min.92) y Manu Justo (Javi Eslava, min.81). Goles: 0-1, min.74: Manu Justo. 0-2, min.89: Javi Eslava. 1-2, min.97: Antonio Sánchez. Árbitro: Sergio Escriche Guzmán, del comité valenciano. Mostró la tarjeta amarilla a los locales José Mas (min.35), Johan Terranova (min.93), Dani Merchán (min.94) y al entrenador Adrián Hernández (min.77) y al visitante Alemanara (min.97). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la octava jornada liguera en el grupo 2 de la Primera RFEF de fútbol que se disputó en el estadio Centenario El Rubial de Águilas ante unos 3.000 espectadores. Un primer tiempo de dominio local sin premio El relato de los datos confirma lo que la pizarra escondió durante más de una hora: el Águilas fue el equipo con más llegada y más peligro, aunque la posesión viviese en el otro bando. Los locales firmaron 15 remates por 10 del Ibiza, dispararon 6 a puerta por 4 y generaron las dos únicas ocasiones claras del encuentro, frente a ninguna de su rival. En el apartado del balón parado, la diferencia fue abismal: 11 córners para el Águilas por solo 2 del Ibiza. El Ibiza, en cambio, administró el cuero —61% de posesión y 465 pases por los 269 del rival— y confió en que su solidez atrás y la figura de su portero resistieran. El guion exigió un contratiempo temprano: el Águilas tuvo que mover el banquillo ya en el minuto 23, con la entrada de Adrián Heredia por el lesionado Sergio Sanchís. Pese a la igualdad en los goles esperados (0,79 del Águilas por 0,73 del Ibiza), el matiz lo marcó quien estuvo bajo palos. Andrés Prieto, portero visitante, completó 5 paradas y firmó un 7,8 de valoración, con un registro de goles evitados de +0,53 que explica por qué el marcador aguantó en blanco tanto tiempo. Diecisiete minutos que lo cambiaron todo El partido se rompió en el 74. Manu Justo, el delantero del Ibiza, definió para el 0-1 en una acción que llegó sin asistencia reseñada. Fue el premio a la constancia visitante y el golpe que obligó al Águilas a lanzarse hacia adelante con todo. El conjunto local se volcó, pero el Ibiza golpeó de nuevo cuando más daño hacía. En el minuto 89, Javier Eslava —que había entrado al campo apenas ocho minutos antes— remató a la red el centro de David Astals para firmar el 0-2. Eslava resolvió su única ocasión con contundencia: un disparo, un gol a puerta y un 7,5 de valoración en un cameo decisivo. Cuando el encuentro parecía sentenciado, el Águilas maquilló el resultado en el minuto 90. Antonio Sánchez, central reconvertido en protagonista ofensivo, recogió la asistencia de José Manuel Raigal para establecer el definitivo 1-2. Fue un consuelo tardío que no alteró el reparto de puntos, pero que dejó patente que los locales nunca dejaron de empujar. Raigal, el faro que mereció más Si hubo un futbolista que merecía otro desenlace, ese fue José Manuel Raigal. El mediapunta del Águilas firmó la mejor nota del partido con un 7,9, repartió la asistencia del gol y fue un incordio constante por banda: 5 pases clave, 17 centros intentados (7 acertados), 5 disparos y la ocasión más clara del equipo, catalogada como ocasión manifiesta. Su registro de goles esperados y asistencias esperadas (0,37 xG y 0,51 xA) retrata a un jugador que estuvo cerca de decidir el partido él solo. A su alrededor brillaron también Javier Castedo, con un 7,3, un palo (el único madero del encuentro lo golpeó el Águilas) y 4 pases clave, y el goleador Antonio Sánchez, que cerró con un 7,6. En defensa, el central José Mas (6,7) aportó 5 despejes y ganó 8 de sus duelos. En el Ibiza, más allá de Prieto y de los dos goleadores, la salida de balón descansó en sus centrales. Erik Ruiz (7,1) y Jérémy Blasco (6,7) combinaron 121 pases entre ambos y acumularon un buen volumen de conducción progresiva, mientras que David Astals (7,2) sumó la asistencia del segundo tanto y 3 pases clave desde una posición adelantada. Lo que deja la clasificación El resultado tiene lecturas opuestas a ambos lados. La UD Ibiza se instala con 13 puntos (4 victorias, 1 empate, 3 derrotas) en la sexta posición del Grupo 2, metida de lleno en la pelea por los puestos de privilegio dentro de un pelotón muy apretado: hasta cuatro equipos comparten esos mismos 13 puntos y el liderato del Villarreal B U23 queda a solo cuatro. Para el CDA Águilas FC, en cambio, la derrota ahonda su crisis. Los de casa siguen con 6 puntos (1 victoria, 3 empates, 4 derrotas) en la 17ª plaza, en zona de descenso, con un balance de 8 goles a favor y 14 en contra que ya es el reflejo de un arranque de curso complicado. Haber generado las mejores ocasiones y acabar sin puntos convierte este revés en doblemente doloroso. Conclusión El 1-2 de Águilas es un recordatorio clásico de la categoría: no basta con merecer, hay que rematar. El Águilas mandó en el juego directo, en los córners y en las ocasiones, pero se topó con un portero inspirado y con un Ibiza frío que esperó su momento y lo aprovechó por partida doble. Eslava, desde el banquillo, firmó la diferencia que separa pelear por el ascenso de mirar hacia abajo.

articles.title: No. 1 Georgia Upset by Auburn on Late FG, Box Score, Player Stats, Highlights & AP Poll Prediction
articles.summary: No. 1 Georgia suffered a 27-24 upset loss at the hands of Auburn in Saturday's SEC clash.
articles.body:
No. 1 Georgia suffered a 27-24 upset loss at the hands of Auburn in Saturday's SEC clash.

Auburn kicker Alex McPherson drilled a 34-yard field goal to give the Tigers a surprising victory as time expired in the fourth quarter.

The Bulldogs suffered their first loss of the season, falling to 6-1.

With a loss to an Auburn squad that entered the contest with a 3-2 record to go along with a 1-2 mark in SEC play, Georgia is expected to fall in the next AP Top 25 poll.

After Texas was upset by unranked Oklahoma on Oct. 10, the Longhorns dropped from No. 1 to No. 7. It isn't hard to imagine the Bulldogs experiencing a similar slide.

Head coach Kirby Smart's squad started off strong on Saturday, holding a 14-7 lead at the end of the first quarter.

Auburn eventually tied the score midway through the second, as Tigers receiver Chas Nimrod made an incredible grab in the end zone.

The Bulldogs attempted to jump in front once again on their next drive, but missed a field goal.

Auburn eventually took its first lead of the game on the team's next possession, as McPherson connected on a 49-yard field goal.

Auburn gained a two-score lead to open the second half, starting the third quarter with a 76-yard drive that ended with a touchdown run by quarterback Byrum Brown.

Georgia cut the deficit to seven points early in the fourth quarter with a field goal, though.

After both teams traded punts, the Bulldogs went on a lengthy touchdown drive of their own. Georgia went 96 yards as Gunner Stockton connected with London Humphreys for a short score.

The Bulldogs' defense forced another Auburn punt, although Stockton fumbled the ball while attempting to lead his squad on a game-winning drive.

The Tigers capitalized on the opportunity, driving down to Georgia's 16-yard line before McPherson's kick sealed the final result.

The Bulldogs finished with 440 total yards, but Stockton's three turnovers were costly and ultimately prevented his team from staying unbeaten.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. Duke Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights

articles.body:
Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels are taking home the Victory Bell for the first time in two years after a 24-20 win over the Duke Blue Devils.

Belichick's Tar Heels entered their matchup against the Blue Devils as 2.5-point underdogs at Wallace Wade Stadium in Durham, North Carolina, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The two universities are less than 10 miles apart, with Duke entering Saturday's rivalry on a two-game winning streak against North Carolina. The teams split their previous four meetings 2-2, with all four games decided by a combined 13 points.

The past did not predict the future Saturday. After Duke scored 20 unanswered points to take a late 20-17 lead, the Tar Heels answered with a go-ahead touchdown before their defense sealed the win with an interception, ending the Blue Devils' comeback attempt.

It was all North Carolina in the first half, with Duke's lone points of the opening 30 minutes coming on defense. Duke safety Andrew Pellicciotta recovered a Tar Heels fumble and returned it for a touchdown.

Leading 17-7 at halftime, North Carolina got on the board in the first quarter when Billy Edwards Jr. found Jordan Shipp on a short pass, followed by Demon June running into the end zone on fourth-and-2.

While Duke added two field goals, its defense held North Carolina to a punt and two turnovers on downs, including a 16-yard loss tackle on the punter after he bobbled the snap.

The stops set the stage for Sheppard to catch a 7-yard touchdown pass for his first score of the game, giving the Blue Devils their first lead at 20-17.

When North Carolina needed an answer, Jaylen McGill rushed for a 24-yard touchdown, giving UNC its first points since the 13:43 mark of the second quarter.

A game-sealing interception by Eget with 14 seconds left secured the win for North Carolina as the Victory Bell changed hands.

North Carolina will host Syracuse next Saturday, with kickoff scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET, while Duke will have a short turnaround, hitting the road for a Friday night showdown against Virginia at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Winners and Losers from Week 7
articles.summary: The nonstop action of a stellar Week 7 slate is fueling a wild, season-shaking day around college football.
articles.body:
The nonstop action of a stellar Week 7 slate is fueling a wild, season-shaking day around college football.

Ohio State picked up a dramatic win at Indiana, while the Arch Manning era at Texas appears to have reached a crossroads after a stunning loss to Florida. And those are simply the highlights of the early window.

The afternoon slate saw Georgia and Alabama fall in rivalries, along with another high-profile QB having a memorable day for the wrong reasons.

And then in prime time, a pair of controversial finishes kept Miami and BYU in the dwindling ranks of the unbeatens.

On the heels of losses to Missouri and South Carolina, Florida knew it would be without starting QB Aaron Philo this week.

Yeah, Texas was struggling. But surely the Horns wouldn't lose at home against a backup, right? Late in the second quarter, they held a 17-3 advantage and hadn't surrendered much of anything to Tramell Jones Jr. and the Gators offense.

The rushing attack came to life, Jones connected on a bunch of third-down passes and UF's defense slammed the door on Manning— potentially for good . Fast-forward to the final whistle, and 24 unanswered points led to a 27-24 victory.

In the coming days, expect a conversation around whether Philo, when healthy, should be the starter over Jones. That's less important right now.

The focus, instead, is how UF stopped its slide with a resilient road win.

Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor emerged as one of the best stories in September, leading the Bulldogs to a flashy 4-0 start. They climbed to 16th in the AP Top 25, matching the program's second-highest ranking of the last decade and poking into the College Football Playoff discussion.

Two weeks ago, however, MSU fell in 56-23 blowout to Alabama. And on Saturday, a Taylor-less offense failed to dent the scoreboard in a 31-0 loss at LSU.

Don't mistake this for an eulogy; Mississippi State is still 4-2 with a defensible path to seven or eight wins.

Nevertheless, the Dawgs' early dreams of an ascent are formally dashed.

By the slimmest of slim margins, Ohio State went to fifth-ranked Indiana and became the first team since 2024 to defeat the Hoosiers.

Clinging to a 19-15 lead in the final minute of regulation, the Buckeyes saw IU receiver Nick Marsh slip beyond any threat of coverage. But as he reeled in a potential game-winning catch, Marsh's left foot touched down out of bounds.

In truly jaw-dropping fashion, Ohio State survived as it snapped a 22-game winning streak for Curt Cignetti and the Hoosiers.

The negative news is OSU quarterback Julian Sayin exited the game and returned to the sideline in a sling. He's set to miss several weeks, and true freshman Luke Fahey is expected to take command of the offense.

But that's a problem for another day. Ohio State is now the Big Ten's team to beat.

During the 2010s in particular, the conference found itself allergic to defense. We regularly saw offenses at Baylor, Oklahoma, Oklahoma State, TCU and Texas Tech hanging 40-some points every game.

Cincinnati and West Virginia put together a throwback performance on Saturday in a chaotic 48-45 affair.

While propelling the Mountaineers to the tight win, WVU quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. threw for 464 yards, rushed for 77 and totaled five scores. The offense racked up 598 yards, its most in an FBS game since 2023—against Cincinnati.

West Virginia needed every bit of that outburst, considering the defense ceded 622 yards. At least the unit managed a key three-and-out that set up Jack Cassidy's 35-yard field goal as time expired, so there was some life.

Neither defense is going to love watching the film, though.

Winner: Get-Right Games for Ole Miss, Texas Tech

The best possible thing that can happen on such a chaotic, upset-filled day is avoiding any shred of drama.

Ole Miss and Texas Tech calmly took care of business.

Star running back Kewan Lacy finally had a big game for Ole Miss, rushing for a season-high 122 yards in a 31-3 rout of 13th-ranked Missouri and former QB Austin Simmons. Makhi Frazier added 101 yards on the ground as Trinidad Chambliss totaled 255 yards and four touchdowns.

Texas Tech, meanwhile, cruised to a 53-25 win opposite an Arizona State program that upset the Red Raiders last season. They roared out to a 33-point halftime lead behind a pick-six and a couple of explosive scores.

Both programs are solidly in the Top 10 at the halfway point, and they won't be lacking confidence after Saturday's comprehensive wins.

The hype is not their fault. That's on us.

Simultaneously, the praise existed for good reason. Arch Manning and Bryce Underwood flashed spectacular talent as high schoolers, then headed to big-brand programs Texas and Michigan, respectively.

Texas had struggled to sustain national relevance—Manning would fix that. Michigan had an atrocious offense in 2024—Underwood would be the solution.

And here we are, 18 games into their tenures as QB1, staring at the end.

Manning's struggles in SEC action have persisted to the point that Texas must seriously consider a change. Michigan hit a breaking point in Week 7, benching Underwood at halftime during an eventual win over Penn State.

The former 5-star quarterbacks, two players tasked with changing the trajectory of their programs, are at risk of losing their jobs for good.

What an afternoon for Auburn and Tennessee, huh? The underdogs pulled off sensational upsets of bitter rivals Georgia and Alabama, respectively.

Georgia, which had notched nine straight wins in the series, will leave its perch atop the AP Top 25. The sky is not falling in Athens, given that UGA is still 6-1, but the schedule doesn't get easier with rival Florida, Ole Miss and Mizzou awaiting the Dawgs following an open weekend.

Alabama's outlook is more nerve-wracking since the Crimson Tide—which fell to UGA last week—dipped to 5-2. Although three-loss teams can make the 12-team CFP, that's not a comfortable spot. LSU and Auburn remain on Bama's docket.

Additionally, every team in the SEC has dropped a conference game. The league is headed for a beautiful six-week frenzy to decide the standings.

"I win," Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said. "Google me."

That simple sentence became a cult classic last season as the Hoosiers won a remarkable national championship. They punched a CFP ticket in Cignetti's debut season, then won it all in Year 2.

Kentucky isn't destined to follow a similar path. But if the Cats are morphing into a national threat, we'll remember what Will Stein said at his first SEC Media Days.

Why can the program win? " Because of me ," he said.

Sealed by Jordan Casteel's late pick-six, Kentucky held off Oklahoma 21-13. The defense snatched four interceptions in the victory, and the Cats improved to 6-1 with a game against Vanderbilt—winless in SEC play—up next.

At this moment—just minutes after the review was completed—this victory from Miami is very much in question.

First, a shaky-at-best holding call negated a Hail Mary touchdown on 4th-and-21 for Florida State. On the next snap, a shaky-at-best replay determination that Bryce Fitzgerald intercepted a pass—and FSU receiver Duce Robinson did not catch it—iced a dramatic 43-35 double-overtime rivalry win for Miami.

That was, without question, a gift for Miami—even as the Hurricanes may have stopped a potential game-tying two-point conversion anyway. They were nowhere close to their best Saturday night.

Due to the upsets everywhere else, the injury-riddled 'Canes have a real—and exceptionally fortunate—crack at becoming the nation's top-ranked team in Week 8.

Oh, you thought the ref show was over? Hold my adult beverage.

Clinging to a 28-24 advantage with four seconds left in regulation, BYU needed one final stop to upset Notre Dame. CJ Carr's pass dropped to the ground, igniting a raucous celebration for the home crowd.

Not only did ND have a legitimate argument for a defensive pass interference, there was clearly one second left on the clock when the ball hit the ground.

BYU played an awesome game. That should not be diminished.

As double-digit underdogs, the Cougars defied the odds and built an 11-point halftime lead. Notre Dame scored the next 14, but Bear Bachmeier found Walker Lyons for the go-ahead score late in the fourth quarter.

In the same breath, it's fair to mention that BYU, like Miami, benefited from a considerable break at a decisive moment.

articles.title: Keelon Russell, Alabama vs. Tennessee Box Score, Stats, Highlights & Prediction for Top 25 AP Poll
articles.summary: The No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide were stunned by the No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers on the road, suffering a 26-10 defeat in Knoxville.
articles.body:
The No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide were stunned by the No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers on the road, suffering a 26-10 defeat in Knoxville.

Keelon Russell and the Tide's offense struggled to find their rhythm, turning in a shaky performance as Tennessee capitalized on Alabama's mistakes to secure a statement win.

The Crimson Tide entered as 7.5-point favorites over the Volunteers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , with both teams entering the matchup with one loss.

Holding Alabama's offense to just 201 total yards while forcing four turnovers proved too much for the Crimson Tide to overcome, dropping them to 5-2 on the season.

2. (14) Tennessee: 3-1 (CONF), 6-1 (OVR)

8. (16) Mississippi St.: 2-2 (CONF), 4-2 (OVR)

14. South Carolina: 1-3 (CONF), 3-3 (OVR)

Alabama may have caught a break, losing on one of the most upset-heavy days of the college football season. No. 1 Georgia and No. 7 Texas both fell to unranked opponents, while No. 5 Indiana suffered its first loss of the season and Mississippi State fell to lower-ranked LSU.

The loss marks Alabama's second of the season, following a 20-17 defeat against Georgia last week, as the Crimson Tide fall in back-to-back games.

The AP Top 25 poll will certainly see a drastic shift in rankings, with Alabama potentially falling out of the top 10 amid big wins from lower-ranked Ole Miss, LSU and Texas Tech.

The first half was full of chaos between the Crimson Tide and Volunteers.

Alabama was held scoreless in the first quarter, committing two turnovers — a sack-fumble and an interception — in a disastrous opening quarter for Russell.

Meanwhile, Tennessee kicked field goals on its first three possessions to take a 9-0 lead.

The second quarter was just as turbulent, this time with the Volunteers suffering from the same miscues.

After three straight punts, MacIntyre threw an interception at Tennessee's own 28-yard line, which Alabama turned into a score on the very next play, with Russell rushing up the middle for a touchdown.

The Volunteers answered with their fourth field goal of the first half before forcing Alabama to punt on fourth-and-4.

On the punt return, Tennessee's returner could not pick the ball up in a crowd of Crimson, giving Alabama possession on the Volunteers' 23-yard line. Alabama returned the favor, fumbling on fourth-and-1 on its next possession.

Bama added a field goal before the end of the second quarter to trail 12-10 at halftime.

The second half was much cleaner for both teams, as Tennessee's DeSean Bishop ran in a 5-yard touchdown to give the Volunteers a 19-10 lead heading into the fourth quarter.

A fourth-quarter touchdown, Bishop's second of the game, and Russell's second interception sealed the outcome as Tennessee walked away with a 16-point win.

Alabama will host the Texas A&M Aggies next Saturday, while Tennessee hits the road to face the South Carolina Gamecocks. Both games are scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff.

articles.title: Juan Manuel Rodríguez: "Soy el responsable de todo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico pide paciencia tras el 0-3 ante el Castellón y reclama unidad
articles.summary: El técnico pide paciencia tras el 0-3 ante el Castellón y reclama unidad
articles.body: El estreno de Juan Manuel Rodríguez en el banquillo de la UD Las Palmas terminó con una dura derrota por 0-3 ante el Castellón y protestas de la afición contra Miguel Ángel Ramírez. El técnico amarillo asumió la responsabilidad y pidió confianza para cambiar la dinámica del equipo. "Estoy descontento y triste con el resultado, pero este equipo no ha bajado los brazos", defendió Rodríguez, que señaló los dos goles encajados en la primera parte y la lesión de Iñaki González como factores que condicionaron el encuentro. No obstante, fue contundente: "La culpa de perder es nuestra, y yo me pongo el primero. Soy el responsable directo de todo". El entrenador reconoció el enfado de la grada: "Si no se molesta sería ilógico», aunque pidió evitar divisiones. "La afición es siempre nuestro número 12", afirmó. También reclamó paciencia y destacó la importancia de mejorar en las acciones a balón parado: "En Segunda División a balón parado se ganan muchos partidos". Álex Suárez fue más duro con la plantilla: "Si tienen que insultar, que nos insulten a los jugadores. El problema está en el campo, nosotros los jugadores, no está arriba ni en el banquillo". El defensa pidió aceptar las críticas y trabajar para revertir la situación. Enzo Loiodice reconoció que están "hundidos" y pidió unidad, mientras que Manu Fuster admitió que el equipo debe cambiar su imagen. "Hoy es culpa de los jugadores, es culpa nuestra y ya está. Toca dar la cara el próximo día", señaló el atacante. La UD Las Palmas afronta ahora el reto de reaccionar tras una derrota que ha aumentado el malestar de su afición y que deja a Juan Manuel Rodríguez con la tarea de recuperar la confianza y el rendimiento del equipo.

articles.title: Kalen DeBoer Warns Alabama 'It's Going to Be Really Uncomfortable' After Tennessee Upset Loss
articles.summary: Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer plans to take a tougher approach with his team moving forward after the No. 6 Crimson Tide suffered a 26-10 loss to No. 14 Tennessee on Saturday.
articles.body:
Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer plans to take a tougher approach with his team moving forward after the No. 6 Crimson Tide suffered a 26-10 loss to No. 14 Tennessee on Saturday.

"It's going to be really uncomfortable," DeBoer said, according to 247Sports' Mike Rodak .

"We've been through this before and we got it done," he added, per Rodak . "I told the guys, this is a team that can do it."

The defeat marked Alabama's second consecutive loss following a 5-0 start to the season.

In 2025, the Crimson Tide's second defeat of the year came in their 10th game.

DeBoer's squad kept pace with Tennessee through the first two quarters on Saturday, only trailing 12-10 at halftime of the contest.

Still, the Volunteers took a two-score lead with a 60-yard touchdown drive during their first possession of the third quarter and never looked back. Alabama was held scoreless in the second half.

With it's worth noting that the Crimson Tide were without key contributors including wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and center Racin Delgatty due to injuries , their offensive struggles against the Volunteers were disappointing regardless.

Alabama committed four turnovers and compiled a mere 201 total yards as a team, converting two of 13 opportunities on third down and one of three chances on fourth down.

Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell finished 19-of-29 for 147 yards and two interceptions. Russell added a touchdown on the ground, but also lost a fumble.

DeBoer will attempt to help Alabama get back on track in its next matchup, a clash with Texas A&M on Oct. 24.

articles.title: There's a crackdown on sports piracy - but is it already out of control?
articles.summary: The sports industry's lucrative business model is being undermined by dodgy TV sticks and illegal streaming links, writes Theo Leggett.
articles.body:
"Football's Gone Round the Spend!" screamed The People newspaper one Sunday in July 1995. It reported breathlessly that three clubs between them were set to pay out more than £20m on new players.

The highlight that summer was the transfer of Stan Collymore from Nottingham Forest to Liverpool for a British record fee of £8.5m.

That number might not seem too impressive today, in an age when £100m transfers are almost commonplace. But at the time it was seismic stuff, and it symbolised the conversion of football from sport into big business.

All of this had been made possible in the early 1990s by the creation of the Premier League, and its initial TV deal with the broadcaster Sky, which paid more than £300m for five years of rights. The agreement put live top-tier football behind a TV paywall for the first time.

It was a lucrative model, one that other leading championships in motorsport, rugby, golf and cricket would later seek to replicate.

But now, that model is coming under pressure. Piracy has become endemic in British sports: around half of sports fans now admit to using what they might euphemistically call "alternative" means to watch paywalled material, according to the consultancy Ampere Analysis.

And this summer saw signs of a clampdown.

In August, a man in Lancashire was jailed for six and a half years for running an illegal streaming service that police said had generated almost £1m in illicit profits. In June, a postman from Pembrokeshire was jailed for over three years for selling illegal subscriptions and supplying pirate software to nearly 2,000 people.

A third man, from Merseyside, received a suspended 32-month sentence in August for similar offences. Several pubs have been fined thousands of pounds for screening matches illegally.

TV companies that have paid huge sums for exclusive rights to high-profile sports are having to work harder than ever to protect their investments. To some extent, broadcasters used to see copyright theft as a cost of doing business: irritating and expensive, but not an existential threat. But now, as advertising revenues fall, and viewers move away from long-term subscription services like Sky or TNT Sports, the industry is getting seriously worried.

There is a great deal at stake. The Premier League alone is a sporting monster. In its most recent deal, it sold its viewing rights to domestic audiences for £6.7bn over four years, with almost as much coming from foreign rights. Armed with bundles of TV cash, clubs have been able to attract the finest players in the world. That in turn has given the league a major international profile.

Although football has been the main beneficiary of paid-for TV in the UK, other competitions such as Formula One, Six Nations rugby and the Wimbledon tennis championships have also commanded very high fees for selling exclusive rights. Live sport on free-to-air television has become increasingly rare.

Yet that wealth could be threatened by a surge in piracy and illegal viewing. The practice is most common among younger, digital-native audiences, who each year become a larger and larger share of sports fans. But many older viewers also seem comfortable with it.

"For 18 to 34-year-olds, it's over 70% who admit to doing this regularly," says Daniel Monaghan, a researcher at Ampere Analysis. "Over half of 35 to 44s admit to doing it, and about a third of those aged 45 to 64."

This year's Champions League final went behind a paywall in the UK for the first time in more than 30 years. Viewers were asked to pay at least £4.99 to watch it, prompting a backlash, including from the then-prime minister, Arsenal fan Sir Keir Starmer.

"Hardworking people shouldn't have to fork out for a subscription to watch this match," he wrote on X.

Many simply refused to pay: 3.7 million IP addresses accessed illegal streams of the match in the UK, according to research carried out by the Gaming Compliance International consultancy, on behalf of the Guardian newspaper. That compared to around seven million people who watched it legally in the UK.

One prolific user of pirate streams is "Kiran", a tech sector worker in his 30s, who prefers not to give his real name. A keen Arsenal fan, he likes to watch Premier League and Champions League games, as well as big matches in Spain's La Liga. He has a paid subscription to TNT Sports, but uses streaming websites to see games that are not available there.

"What it comes down to is the financial side - that's the big one - and ease of access as well," he says. "Getting every single game will cost you hundreds of pounds a year."

Meanwhile the streams he uses are free, with links readily obtainable on social media.

But there's another issue, he says: the famous blackout. Games taking place between 14:45 and 17:15 on a Saturday are not usually screened live in the UK, a decades-old policy designed to protect crowds at lower league matches. But broadcasters outside the UK can and do show those matches, fuelling pirated streams.

"I pretty much got into streaming stuff due to [the blackout]," Kiran says, "and I'd say I sort of did it a bit more as subscriptions got more expensive."

Those searching for pirated material have plenty of options. Streaming links, along with advice on how to avoid their pitfalls, are freely available in online discussion groups. These links, used by Kiran and his friends, have practical downsides – such as frequent buffering or poor quality, or platforms that disappear without warning. In some cases, they can also be used to bombard viewers with explicit ads for porn sites.

Many people prefer to access illegal content with a streaming device, such as an Amazon Fire Stick, a pocket-sized gadget that plugs into a TV. The sticks are legitimate products, but they can also be "sideloaded" with unauthorised software, allowing pirates to mimic the output of legitimate outlets by offering packages of selected channels.

A third option for illicit viewing is to use a virtual private network, or VPN, which effectively allows your computer to pretend it's in a different country, one in which access to sports programming is cheaper than it is in the UK (or totally free).

Earlier this year, the Sports Industry Group found that 58% of fans surveyed considered illegal streaming to be socially acceptable.

That may be because viewers have simply come to resent the amount of money they are expected to pay.

As the government's Intellectual Property Office puts it, "a main driver of illegal content access is the perception of unfair or high pricing for legal services".

A British person wanting to access all live Premier League games, for example, would need subscriptions to both Sky Sports and TNT Sports. Throw in some matches from Spain, or European Champions Cup rugby, and Premier Sports has to be added to the list. Many boxing matches and NFL games are on DAZN. A keen fan could easily end up paying £80 to £100 a month.

Until relatively recently, clamping down on piracy was not seen as a priority by the broadcasters themselves. They were focused on audience growth, and copyright infringement was simply a cost of doing business.

In some parts of the industry, it was even seen as a benefit. In 2013, the then-chief executive of Time Warner, Jeff Bewkes, notoriously welcomed the drama series Game of Thrones becoming the most pirated show in the world. He suggested that the attention generated by illegal viewing was "better than an Emmy" because it helped create buzz and ultimately attract new subscribers.

Now, however, the mood has shifted. Conventional broadcasting is under pressure as advertising revenues fall and viewers move away from long-term subscription services, towards more flexible offers from streaming platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime and Apple TV. Both Sky and TNT Sports have reported losses.

According to a recent report by WPI Economics, illegal sports streaming costs the broadcasting industry about £700m each year.

And piracy is already having impacts on the pitch.

At a conference last year, Tom Burrows, the head of global rights at the sports streaming platform DAZN, described piracy as a "huge problem" for his company, and "almost a crisis for the sports rights industry".

Just months after he made those comments, DAZN agreed to end its deal with the French football league, under which it was allowed to screen the top tier of French football matches within France. The agreement followed a bitter dispute, which focused in part on the streamer's claims the league had not done enough to combat piracy – although subscriber numbers were also understood to be an issue.

Even though DAZN paid a reported €100m (£85m) to end the contract (along with outstanding rights fees worth another €140m), its departure created a hole in the French league's finances. It was left to set up its own streaming service, and the amount of broadcast income fell from roughly €700m per year to €412m this season, according to figures compiled by football-finance.com.

For a European powerhouse like Paris St Germain, with plenty of other revenue sources, this probably matters little. But for smaller teams it has been a serious problem. Angers SCO, a club in the west of France, said last year the affair had cost it €30m over two seasons, and forced it to sell its striker Estéban Lepaul.

It's unlikely that a competition on the scale of the Premier League would lose its broadcaster. But piracy could ultimately limit how much they will be willing to pay in future.

"If you look at the finances of some of the broadcasters, they're losing money," says Kieran Maguire, associate professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool. "Piracy… is taking up a larger and larger share of the revenues that they would anticipate being able to generate through their subscription models. So yes, it is a worry for them."

Daniel Monaghan of Ampere thinks piracy "is at the very least a significant constraint on the sports rights models that have been highly lucrative for broadcasters and rights holders over the last 30 years".

If left unchecked, he thinks this will make it harder for rights holders to generate a return on their investments.

At best this could hamper future growth. At worst it could lead to falling revenues over time, hitting the sports that have benefitted most from the wave of TV money.

In the case of the Premier League, this might just mean fewer blockbuster transfers - but it could also reduce the sum the League gives to the wider football game, from grassroots upwards, which amounted to £1.6bn over the three years to 2025.

A key part of the solution, according to the industry-funded Federation Against Copyright Theft (Fact), is changing attitudes among consumers.

Nick Sumner, the organisation's investigations manager, insists piracy is not a victimless crime. "Organised crime is behind this, and they want to make money by any means possible," he explains.

It also leaves users at risk of fraud, he warns. "They capture… a lot of personal data, which they can then sell for criminal gain."

Broadcasters and sporting bodies have been working hard to shut off illegal online streams. Hundreds of thousands are taken down each year. But tackling them is, as Monaghan puts it, like whack-a-mole: "Some get taken down, others come up, often in different countries."

In the UK, downloading or streaming pirated content can be a crime. Yet the chances of viewers themselves being prosecuted for watching a cheeky Saturday game on a pirate stream are extremely low.

The £5 coffee that tells a story of global economic turmoil

Europe's car makers are in crisis. Will the threat of war rescue them?

Why some experts increasingly fear AI will take over

Nick Sumner of Fact says the current priority is to educate people about the risks of piracy - but he conspicuously stops short of ruling out a more punitive future policy.

"There are crimes being committed here," he says.

So it is possible that viewers of illicit material just might one day find themselves in expensive legal trouble.

However, the sheer scale of a major clampdown would present a formidable challenge, and could generate resentment. There would be no guarantees that those watching illegally today would take out legitimate subscriptions tomorrow.

articles.title: El Barça, obligado a pasar la noche en Sevilla debido al temporal
articles.standfirst: La expedición estuvo más de dos horas en el avión esperando un visto bueno que no llegó
articles.summary: La expedición estuvo más de dos horas en el avión esperando un visto bueno que no llegó
articles.body: La expedición del Barça no pudo regresar tras el partido a Barcelona, tal y como tenía previsto. Los jugadores tuvieron que pasar la noche en un hotel de Sevilla ante la imposibilidad de viajar debido a la alerta meteorológica que está afectando a numerosas partes de España. Antes de cancelarse el viaje de manera definitiva, la plantilla vivió una eterna espera. Los jugadores, ya acomodados a bordo del avión chárter en el aeropuerto San Pablo de Sevilla, vieron cómo se retrasaba el despegue en varias ocasiones debido al temporal. Estuvieron aguardando en el aparato durante dos horas buscando una autorización para volar que nunca llegó. Fue el propio club el que lo comunicó mediante un mensaje en X cerca de las dos de la madrugada. La cancelación del vuelo se enmarca en un contexto de alerta máxima en Cataluña. Horas antes del bloqueo en el aeropuerto, Protección Civil ya había activado este sábado las alarmas por temporal en varias zonas ante una previsión de lluvias torrenciales que amenazaban con acumular hasta 100 litros por metro cuadrado. El cambio de planes llega justo antes de una semana clave para los de Flick, que el martes rinden visita en Champions al PSG y el domingo reciben en LaLiga al Real Madrid.

articles.title: Indiana's Charlie Becker Apologizes to Ryan Day for Mocking OSU in Celebration Last Season in Video
articles.summary: Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker apologized to Ohio State head coach Ryan Day after the Hoosiers' 19-15 home loss to the Buckeyes on Saturday for mocking OSU in a celebration last season after the Big Ten Championship Game.
articles.body:
Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker apologized to Ohio State head coach Ryan Day after the Hoosiers' 19-15 home loss to the Buckeyes on Saturday for mocking OSU in a celebration last season after the Big Ten Championship Game.

Indiana beat Ohio State 13-10 last December to win the Big Ten Championship. Becker was exceptional, catching six passes for 126 yards. Afterward, cameras caught Becker doing his own version of the "O-H-I-O" chant (O-H-F-U).

Everything seems OK between Becker and Day based on their postgame interaction.

As for the game, Becker was the star with nine catches for 165 yards, but OSU emerged victorious in part because wideout Jeremiah Smith caught an incredible 38-yard TD pass.

Indiana stormed back and was very close to taking the lead late after QB Josh Hoover found wideout Nick Marsh in the end zone, but he landed just out of bounds.

OSU (6-1 overall, 4-0 Big Ten) will have a bye week before it visits USC on Halloween. Indiana (6-1 overall, 3-1 Big Ten) will travel to face Michigan next Saturday.

articles.title: Jordan Carrillo “revive” con Chivas: entra en un momento crítico y anota su primer gol contra Tigres
articles.standfirst: El joven mexicano ha ingresado de cambio para ser el que cambió el partido para Gabriel Milito
articles.summary: El joven mexicano ha ingresado de cambio para ser el que cambió el partido para Gabriel Milito
articles.body: Jordan Carrillo ha revivido en el momento que las Chivas de Gabriel Milito más lo necesitaban y es que después de llegar como uno de los mejores futbolistas del Clausura 2026 con los Pumas en donde fue pieza clave para Efraín Juárez y que el equipo auriazul pudiera disputar una Final, pero que todavía quedaba a deber cuando ingresaba con la escuadra rojiblanca. Sin embargo, después de 12 juegos de Chivas en el Apertura 2026, en los que no ha visto acción en todos, entró como revulsivo para presionar a Tigres que se había quedado con un hombre menos por la expulsión de Juan Brunetta y necesitaban empatar para no perder lugares en la tabla generar y apareció Jordan Carrillo cuando más lo necesitaban. Desde que Jordan Carrillo llegó a las Chivas le había costado mantener el ritmo que tuvo el semestre pasado con los Pumas de Efraín Juárez por lo que de a poco fue siendo relegado a la banca, pero ante múltiples lesiones ha tenido nuevamente una oportunidad con el Guadalajara. Fue al minuto 76' que las Chivas encontraron su ansiado gol luego de un centro que remataron y Jordan Carrillo se estiró para desviar al balón y mandarlo al fondo de las redes para que el Estadio Akron explotara y así las Chivas no dejaran ir puntos en su casa. Este gol representa una gran motivación para Jordan Carrillo ante las múltiples ausencias por lo que podría comenzar a recibir más minutos y así demsotrar que puede elevar su nivel como en el semestre pasado que fue fundamental para que los Pumas disputaran la Gran Final ante Cruz Azul. Y es que la comparativa con lo hecho el semestre anterior y ahora con las Chivas ha comenzado a despertar un amplio debate sobre Jordan Carrillo de si estaba a la altura de portar la camiseta rojiblanca o si hay más presión en el Guadalajara que no le permite despuntar. articles.title: 'Every F--king Play,' Jeremiah Smith Calls Out Indiana's Double-Teams in Viral OSU Locker-Room Video
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith helped lead the No. 4 Buckeyes to a 19-15 road win over No. 5 Indiana on Saturday thanks in part to this great 38-yard touchdown catch on fourth down in the fourth quarter:
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith helped lead the No. 4 Buckeyes to a 19-15 road win over No. 5 Indiana on Saturday thanks in part to this great 38-yard touchdown catch on fourth down in the fourth quarter:

Smith provided his thoughts after the game via a live stream on OSU cornerback Devin Sanchez's Instagram (h/t ESPN ):

"They doubled teamed me every f--king play," Smith said.

Smith entered the day with 48 catches for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. He was slowed down somewhat (four catches for 68 yards) but ultimately came through when his team needed him most.

He and the Buckeyes will have next week off before visiting USC on Halloween.

articles.title: No. 3 Miami Avoids FSU Upset as Hail Mary Negated in 2OT, Toney's Box Score Stats Amid Heisman Race
articles.summary: No. 3 Miami football avoided a near upset against arch-rival Florida State on Saturday evening before holding on for a 43-35 double overtime win.
articles.body:
No. 3 Miami football avoided a near upset against arch-rival Florida State on Saturday evening before holding on for a 43-35 double overtime win.

FSU faced a 4th-and-21 from the Miami 36-yard line in double overtime, needing a first down to keep the game alive. Quarterback Ashton Daniels heaved a pass to the end zone, and wide receiver Micahi Danzy was there for the touchdown. However, FSU left tackle Xavier Chaplin was called for holding, and FSU got pushed back 10 yards.

Once again, Daniels threw a pass to the end zone. This time, wide receiver Duce Robinson and defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald fought for the ball in the air. Ultimately, officials deemed that Fitzgerald came away with the interception, and a review upheld the ruling.

Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney also showcased why he's one of the best college football players in the country and a Heisman Trophy candidate en route to leading the No. 3 Hurricanes to a 43-35 double overtime victory at home against arch-rival Florida State.

In addition to his tremendous pass-catching, Toney rushed for 31 yards on two carries and found wide receiver Cooper Barkate with a pass for a two-point conversion to give Miami a 43-35 lead in double OT.

Toney scored his first touchdown in the second quarter after quarterback Darius Mensah found him for 14 yards to put Miami up 13-7.

The sophomore scored his second touchdown in double overtime on a three-yarder and then unleashed the two-point conversion pass.

Toney has now caught 50 passes for 758 yards and eight touchdowns in six games.

FSU gave Miami all it could handle and took a 21-14 lead in the third quarter after Daniels found Quintrevion Wisner for a 28-yard score.

However, Miami responded with a pair of three-yard touchdowns courtesy of a Javian Mallory run and an Elija Lofton reception.

FSU immediately tied the game, though, after Daniels hit Robinson for 75 yards.

The two teams traded touchdowns in overtime. FSU started with Robinson's 20-yard touchdown catch, but Miami got a score when Mallory ran it in from 25 yards.

In the end, the 'Canes held on for the win thanks in part to Toney, who's on track to be heading to New York as a Heisman finalist in December.

articles.title: Notre Dame vs. BYU Box Score, Stats, Highlights for CJ Carr, Marcus Freeman's Dramatic Loss
articles.summary: No. 2 Notre Dame narrowly fell to No. 8 BYU by the final score of 28-24 at LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday night.
articles.body:
No. 2 Notre Dame narrowly fell to No. 8 BYU by the final score of 28-24 at LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday night.

With the Fighting Irish attempting to score a go-ahead touchdown on the final play of the fourth quarter, a pass into the end zone by CJ Carr fell incomplete.

Head coach Marcus Freeman's squad fell to 6-1, as their 16-game win streak dating back to last season officially came to an end.

BYU held an early edge in Saturday's contest, leading 7-3 at the end of the first quarter.

Notre Dame jumped in front near the start of the second, as Nolan James Jr. picked up an eight-yard rushing touchdown.

The Cougars found the end zone on each of their next two drives to take a 21-10 lead, though.

Notre Dame drove into BYU's red zone towards the end of the first half, but Carr fumbled while attempting to spike the ball and prevented his squad from scoring.

The Cougars maintained a 21-10 edge at halftime.

BYU started to make mistakes in the third quarter, beginning with a muffed punt that set up Notre Dame for a field goal.

The Cougars then attempted a fake punt at their own 28-yard line during their next possession, which was stopped by the Fighting Irish.

Notre Dame followed it up with another field goal, cutting the deficit to 21-16.

BYU's offense failed to respond, resulting in a lead change after the Fighting Irish marched down the field and scored with a three-yard rushing touchdown by Jonaz Walton.

Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier was picked off on the team's next possession, but BYU's defense forced a Notre Dame punt.

Bachmeier capitalized on his second opportunity by leading his team on a 10-play, 55-yard drive that was capped off by a short touchdown pass to Walker Lyons.

Notre Dame drove down to BYU's eight-yard line on its final possession, but couldn't score before time expired to seal the final result.

articles.title: ‘It’s time’: Texas coach sparks reactions as he considers benching Arch Manning
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns opened the season as the No. 1 team in the country, but two straight losses have put their College Football Playoff hopes in serious jeop...
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns opened the season as the No. 1 team in the country, but two straight losses have put their College Football Playoff hopes in serious jeopardy. And with Arch Manning struggling, head coach Steve Sarkisian isn't ruling out a quarterback change.

Following Saturday's home loss to the Florida Gators, Sarkisian was asked whether he had considered replacing Manning, and he made it clear that nothing is off the table. Needless to say, his comments got plenty of people talking.

Texas built a 17-3 lead over Florida on Saturday, thanks in part to a 63-yard punt return touchdown from Ryan Niblett. But the Gators, playing with backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. in his first career start, answered with 24 straight points on their way to a 27-24 upset.

Manning went 14-for-20 for 173 yards and a touchdown, but he also lost a fumble that all but sealed the loss. That came just one week after his late interception helped Oklahoma beat Texas in regulation.

Manning has also thrown for more than 250 yards in just one of his last five games. Now 4-2, Texas still has Ole Miss, Mississippi State, Missouri, and LSU on the schedule over the next four weeks.

Asked after the game if he would consider a change at quarterback, Sarkisian left the door open.

"We're not playing good offensive football right now, so everything is going to be evaluated," Sarkisian said, via On3 .

If Texas does make a move, the next man up would be redshirt freshman K.J. Lacey, a former four-star recruit who has played in two games this season. Sarkisian also didn't hold back about his team's performance as a whole.

"Obviously we're extremely disappointed. We didn't play very good football today outside of the first quarter," Sarkisian said, via Inside Texas . "Very disappointed, but we'll work and get back. We've got a better team than how we're playing right now. It's my job to figure out how to get us to play closer to our potential."

Benching Manning, who entered the season as the favorite to go No. 1 overall in the 2027 NFL Draft, would be a stunning move. But it certainly sounds like it's on the table.

"He's benched," wrote Big Cat of Barstool Sports.

"Anybody predict Arch might get *benched* before the season started?" wrote Ringer editor Bryan Curtis .

"Could Arch march to the sideline to watch for at least a week?" wrote Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post.

"He should. He benched Ewers for less," wrote Dallas Cowboys writer Clarence Hill Jr ., adding "it's time" in another post .

"We can't put it all on Arch… Situational football has to be questioned as well…," wrote Dez Bryant .

"Honestly, benching Arch and seeing if KJ can spark the offense might be the only move he has. It's desperate, but they are desperate at this point," wrote longtime football writer Mike Herndon .

Clearly, whether it's Manning or Sarkisian taking the blame, the pressure in Austin is only going to keep building.

articles.title: Oklahoma’s John Mateer throws away another game with brutal interception
articles.summary: Oklahoma football welcomed the Kentucky Wildcats to Norman, Oklahoma in a sneaky-tough game that came after coach Brent Venables was patted on the back for h...
articles.body:
Oklahoma football welcomed the Kentucky Wildcats to Norman, Oklahoma in a sneaky-tough game that came after coach Brent Venables was patted on the back for his win over Texas. Oklahoma legend Gerald McCoy was among those trolling the Longhorns after the Sooners' big win, but the tables turned against Kentucky as quarterback John Mateer made another egregious error.

Mateer's Sooners trailed by one point with 1:25 left on the clock on their side of the field. Mateer took a deep drop, looked over the middle and threw it late into double coverage as Jordan Castell made an interception that he returned for a touchdown, extending the Wildcats' late lead to 21-13.

The Wildcats held on for a 21-13 victory in hostile territory, sending Mateer and Venables' team to 3-3 and likely ending their College Football Playoff hopes. It was a bitter pill for Mateer and the Sooners to swallow, one week after their biggest win of the season. Kentucky scored 14 fourth quarter points to steal the win, shocking the Vegas oddsmakers on a day when they recorded less than 250 yards.

Mateer, who's been blasted by Skip Bayless for his recent mistakes , ended up with 270 yards passing and a touchdown, but three interceptions continued his startling trend of being careless with the football in the worst possible moments.

The Sooners got nearly 200 yards rushing combined from Isaiah Sategna III and Manny Choice, but couldn't cash in with points. Mateer's job seemed safe after the Texas upset, but now appears on shaky ground once again as the Sooners will look to turn the page against Mississippi State in Week 8.

articles.title: 5 instant reactions to Notre Dame’s comeback bid falling short vs. BYU
articles.summary: Notre Dame football joined multiple teams getting upset on Saturday, and here are five instant reactions to the Irish losing.
articles.body:
Notre Dame football suffered its first loss of the season on Saturday night , falling on the road to BYU , 28-24.

The Irish found themselves down 21-10 at halftime, and stormed back to take a 24-21 lead midway through the fourth quarter. Unfortunately, Notre Dame couldn't finish off the comeback, as the Cougars scored with under two minutes left and the last-second touchdown pass attempt was incomplete.

Notre Dame now is 6-1, and without a game next weekend. It's going to be a tough two weeks as this loss will be on their minds the whole time. Speaking of what's on mind, here are five instant reactions to the Irish getting upset by BYU.

This is one that the Irish would love to have back, as they had uncharacteristic mistakes that ultimately cost them. The four penalties for 40-yards wasn't much, but the way they happened made significant impacts. Boubacar Traore was flagged for a targeting, which was upheld and he was disqualified during the first drive of the game. It was the right call, but a costly one. There were more aspects of this that I'll touch on below, as this one will sting for a while.

Carr almost redeemed himself with a game-winning drive, but his pass couldn't find Jordan Faison in the end zone. On the night he'd throw for 261-yards, but it took him 49 attempts without throwing a touchdown pass. Carr missed multiple open receivers, passes that he normally makes. The fumble at the end of the first half was costly, as points could have turned the tide in the end. It was a terrible game for Carr to have his worst one of the season.

Chris Ash's struggles against top teams continues

For much of the second half, it looked like Ash had figured out the BYU offense and was able to stop them. However, when it counted the most, on the final drive, he couldn't find a way to slow down the Cougars. As Pete Sampson shared during the game, Ash's defense against top-20 opponents has not been good, as he met his average of 28 points allowed. It's games like these that define a program, and right now, it hasn't been good enough.

Nolan James Jr. was hot early, so it made sense to stay with him. However, we've seen Jonaz Walton enter the game later and run wild, but he didn't get his chances tonight. He's finished with just 5 carries for 17-yards, and while he did score, it left many wondering why such a small amount of carries.

The loss hurts, but Notre Dame is still in the running for the College Football Playoff

Look around college football today, Georgia , Alabama , Texas , Indiana and now the Irish all lost, every one of the ranked inside the top-10. It's not the end of the world in the 12-team College Football Playoff, but it does make the margin for error much smaller. Notre Dame does not want a 2025-situation to happen again, so beating Miami and SMU is a must.
